﻿Stage37-NEW-INPUT-DELTA-AUDIT-229BT — seven-length radical cutoff and uniform divisor-fiber sector disposal
STATUS: POST_229BS_SEVEN_PHYSICAL_LENGTH_UNIFORM_FIXED_VALUE_FIBERS_PROVED / SEVEN_SQUAREFREE_RADICAL_FIXED_VALUE_FIBERS_PROVED / ONE_THIRD_MINUS_DELTA_LOW_RADICAL_UNION_POWER_SAVING_PROVED / EXACT_HARD_SEVEN_RADICAL_SOURCE_REDUCTION / WEIGHTED_RADICAL_NEGATIVE_MOMENT_PROVED / NO_LARGE_SF_G0_TAIL_SOLUTION / GLOBAL_CREDIT=0 / NO_REOPEN
TYPE: whole-physical exact divisor-factorization count, uniform smooth-support receiver, scoped power-saving sector disposal, radical-height distribution and theorem-input narrowing.
CARD_DOC_ID=1Y-6M5YndDxZJKj95-0oNQPmlU3x_TyL3hz6PcaiVPYg
OPERATIONAL_AUTHORITY=M3-T11-229; LATEST_MATHEMATICAL_CONSTRUCTION=M3-T11-228; M3-T11-230 NOT_ISSUED; PRIMARY_GATE=M3-T11-GATE-001 OPEN; GLOBAL_COUNTING_CREDIT=0; P_OVER_M3_LIMIT_PROVED=false; PRODUCTION HOLD.


1. Source and conventions
Use exactly the current positive primitive Stage37 physical endpoints P, all original selector conditions, original canonical orientation and R(P)<=B. The seven positive integral physical lengths are
  L(P)=(e,x,y,z,U,V,R),                                (229BT.1)
with
  e²+x²=U²,  e²+y²=V²,  x²+y²=z²,  e²+z²=R².        (229BT.2)
All seven lengths are <=R<=B. No perfect cuboid is assumed to exist; every counting statement is conditional on such physical points and remains valid for empty sets. Write rad(n)=product of DISTINCT prime divisors n, with rad(1)=1; this is NOT sf(n), the squarefree kernel with odd valuations.
Retain 229BQ's uniform prescribed-prime-support lemma: for fixed constants A,C, number of n<=B^A with every prime divisor in a specified integer r<=B^C is B^o(1), uniformly in r. Retain 229BR's fixed-e, fixed-R proofs and 229BS's finite-fiber transfer. All new bounds below are uniform in exact integer length values and in canonical physical masks.


2. New seven-length fixed-value divisor lemma
CLAIM 229BT.3. For EACH L in {e,x,y,z,U,V,R}, uniformly for integer 1<=ell<=B,
  #{P:R(P)<=B, L(P)=ell} <= B^o(1).                (229BT.3)
The primitive restrictions and any additional Stage37 selectors only DECREASE these counts. This is a whole-physical bound, not a generic-fiber or reduced-scale estimate.
We prove all seven directly. Set D_B=max_{1<=n<=B} tau(n²)=B^o(1) by the standard divisor bound; for fixed integer hypotenuse n, the number of ordered positive representations s²+t²=n² is <=r_2(n²)<=4tau(n²)<=4D_B.
FIX e=ell. The factorizations
  (U-x)(U+x)=e²;  (V-y)(V+y)=e²
yield at most tau(e²)² choices for (x,U,y,V), and then positive z and R are uniquely determined if integral. Bound D_B².
FIX x=ell. The factorizations
  (U-e)(U+e)=x²;  (z-y)(z+y)=x²
yield at most tau(x²)² choices for (e,U,y,z); then V,R are unique if integral. Bound D_B².
FIX y=ell. The factorizations
  (V-e)(V+e)=y²;  (z-x)(z+x)=y²
yield at most tau(y²)² choices for (e,V,x,z); then U,R are unique if integral. Bound D_B².
FIX z=ell. The factorization (R-e)(R+e)=z² gives at most tau(z²) choices for (e,R); independently the positive representations x²+y²=z² are at most 4tau(z²). Remaining U,V forced. Bound 4D_B².
FIX U=ell. Positive solutions e²+x²=U² number at most 4tau(U²). For each such e, (V-y)(V+y)=e² gives at most tau(e²) choices for y,V; z,R are then forced. Bound 4D_B².
FIX V=ell. Positive solutions e²+y²=V² number at most 4tau(V²). For each e, (U-x)(U+x)=e² gives at most tau(e²) choices for x,U; z,R then forced. Bound 4D_B².
FIX R=ell. Positive solutions e²+z²=R² number at most 4tau(R²). For each e, the two face factorizations above yield at most tau(e²)² pairs (x,U),(y,V). Bound 4D_B³.
Uniform maximum 4D_B³=B^o. All parity checks, relative coprimalities, d0/h factors, positivity, canonicalization, and four simultaneous-square conditions are checked, never suppressed as independence hypotheses. This completes 229BT.3.


3. Seven radical fixed-fiber theorem and minimum-radical scalar
For any L in the seven lengths, fix s=rad(L(P)) (s squarefree, 1<=s<=B). Then each possible L(P)<=B has prime factors supported on s. By 229BQ there are B^o possible L-values uniformly in s; by 229BT.3 each yields B^o physical points. Therefore
  #{P:R<=B, rad(L(P))=s} <= B^o(1),                (229BT.4)
uniformly for all seven L and all squarefree s.
Define the new single-valued extremal scalar
  k_7(P)=min{rad(e),rad(x),rad(y),rad(z),rad(U),rad(V),rad(R)}.   (229BT.5)
Then 1<=k_7(P)<=B, k_7(P) is squarefree, and any fiber k_7(P)=s is covered by at most seven events rad(L(P))=s. Thus
  #{P:R<=B,k_7(P)=s} <= 7 B^o(1)=B^o(1).         (229BT.6)
No independence is used or claimed. Since k_7 only records the minimum physical prime support, it does NOT preserve sf(G0)>threshold as an equivalent or implied k_7>threshold condition.


4. Actual quantitative global low-radical sector bound
For every 1<=T<=B, summing 229BT.6 over s<=T gives
  #{P:R<=B,k_7(P)<=T} <= T B^o(1).              (229BT.7)
Equivalently, the UNION over all seven L of {rad(L)<=T} has this bound. The bound is uniform over all original primitive positive physical endpoints and all Stage37 selectors; it applies without imposing the large-sf(G0) restriction.
For any FIXED delta with 0<delta<1/3, choose T=B^(1/3-delta). Then for any fixed 0<epsilon<delta and sufficiently large B,
  #{P:R<=B,k_7(P)<=B^(1/3-delta)}
    <<_epsilon B^(1/3-delta+epsilon) = o(B^(1/3)). (229BT.8)
This is a genuine SCOPED power-saving estimate for seven simultaneous low-radical sectors, not a claim that the whole endpoint population has this bound.
The disposed sector contains the usual short-length sectors L<=T, but is potentially larger: L may be far above T while rad(L)<=T when repeated prime powers occur. No claim of actual nonempty physical examples is needed.


5. Exact narrowed preferred large-sf source
Retain the authority's original physical source
  S_B(delta)={P:R<=B, P positive primitive with ALL selectors, sf(G0(P))>B^(1/3-delta)},
  G0=gcd(eR,xy)=ab c12 c21.
Define the harder subfamily
  S_B^hard7(delta)={P in S_B(delta):k_7(P)>B^(1/3-delta)}. (229BT.9)
Applying (229BT.8) to the removed subset yields the exact cardinal partition and saving
  |S_B(delta)|=|S_B^hard7(delta)|+O(B^(1/3-delta+o(1))). (229BT.10)
Consequently, for a FIXED delta in (0,1/3), the theorem
  |S_B^hard7(delta)|=o(B^(1/3))                  (229BT.11)
is necessary and sufficient for the original preferred large-sf(G0) tail o(B^(1/3)) at THAT delta. This is a genuine narrower theorem-input domain; it is NOT a proof of (229BT.11).
For the retained 229BR supports T_rho^hard7={rho(P):P in S_B^hard7} and T_sigma^hard7={sigma(P):P in S_B^hard7}, their uniform B^o fibers remain valid by restriction. A fixed-power |T_rho^hard7|<<B^(1/3-epsilon) OR |T_sigma^hard7|<<B^(1/3-epsilon) would suffice for (229BT.11). NEITHER is shown.
The seven high-radical requirements are NOT seven statistically independent constraints, do not change local codimension, and do not warrant multiplication of any sieve densities. They merely remove a provably small global population in ONE count.


6. Weighted radical inverse moment (additional unconditional scoped result)
Because k_7 has B^o fixed-value physical fibers,
  sum_{P:R<=B} k_7(P)^(-s) <= B^o(1) sum_{r=1}^B r^(-s). (229BT.12)
For every fixed s>1, the sum on the right is <=zeta(s), giving
  sum_{P:R<=B} k_7(P)^(-s) = B^o(1).             (229BT.13)
For s=1 the same argument gives B^o(1)*log B=B^o(1). These are weighted statements; NO unweighted total population bound better than O(B^(1+o(1))) follows. Do not infer large-radical savings from inverse moments.


7. New audit outcome and next research contract
RESULT_229BT_SEVEN_FIXED_LENGTH_B_O_PHYSICAL_FIBERS=PROVED_EXACT_DIVISOR_RECONSTRUCTION.
RESULT_229BT_SEVEN_RADICAL_B_O_PHYSICAL_FIBERS=PROVED_FROM_229BQ_SUPPORT_LEMMA.
RESULT_229BT_MIN_SEVEN_RADICAL_SMALL_SECTOR_COUNT=PROVED_O(T_B_O).
RESULT_229BT_GATE_REDUCTION_TO_HARD7=PROVED_EXACT_SCOPED_EQUIVALENCE_UP_TO_o_B13.
RESULT_229BT_NEGATIVE_RADICAL_MOMENT=PROVED_SCOPED.
NEXT_RESEARCH_INPUT_CONTRACT: prove an ACTUAL quantitative selector-aware support bound for retained 229BR rho or sigma, or a direct endpoint count, on the strict S_B^hard7(delta) source with all seven rad(L)>B^(1/3-delta), same original positive primitive Stage37 selectors and exact R<=B; show fixed-power saving B^(1/3-epsilon) or at least o(B^(1/3)). Alternatively find another valid global correlation among the seven physical length prime supports. Do not use height decreases, product of seven local densities, or extrapolate from 229BT.8.

DEPENDENCIES: 229BQ uniform prescribed-prime-support count; 229BR fixed e and R divisor-fibers; 229BS subpower-fiber pushforward, full physical seven-length equations (retained across Stage37). No external theorem beyond standard divisor bound and r_2(n)<=4tau(n); no enumeration or independent hostile audit.

﻿Stage37-NEW-INPUT-DELTA-AUDIT-229BS — subpower-equivalent receiver supports and linear-height radical firewall
STATUS: POST_229BR_UNIFORM_SUBPOWER_RECEIVER_EQUIVALENCE_PROVED / DEGREE_ONE_RAD_E_AND_RAD_R_RECEIVERS_PROVED / EXACT_EDGE_VS_OUTER_SELECTOR_SPLIT_PROVED / ALL_RECEIVER_FIXED_POWER_GATES_EQUIVALENT / NO_ACTUAL_OCCUPIED_VALUE_SAVING / GLOBAL_CREDIT=0 / NO_REOPEN
TYPE: exact cross-receiver value-support transfer; elementary fixed-edge/fixed-outer and uniform smooth-support lemmas; squarefree-kernel selector-loss characterization; strategy firewall
CARD_DOC_ID=1mkN8IrJZi6a4thY1qL77Cuqzq_nTR6p45OIi943dbbI
OPERATIONAL_AUTHORITY=M3-T11-229; LATEST_MATHEMATICAL_CONSTRUCTION=M3-T11-228; M3-T11-230=NOT_ISSUED; PRIMARY_GATE=M3-T11-GATE-001 OPEN; GLOBAL_COUNTING_CREDIT=0; PRODUCTION=HOLD; P_OVER_M3_LIMIT_PROVED=false.


1. Scope and retained source
Fix delta>0 and B>=2. Let S_B(delta) be EXACTLY the current positive primitive physical Stage37 endpoints P satisfying R(P)<=B, ALL original face and space selectors, and sf(G0(P))>B^(1/3-delta), with G0=gcd(eR,xy)=ab c12 c21. No relaxation of source, height, or primitivity is made.
Retain 229BR: rho(P)=rad(Phi(P))<=B^(5/2)/(2sqrt2), sigma(P)=rad(e(P)R(P))<=B^2, and uniform B^o(1) physical fibers for BOTH scalars, with sf(G0)|rho and sf(G0)|sigma. Retain 229BQ uniform bounded-support smooth-number lemma; 229BR independent fixed-edge divisor count and fixed-R divisor count.
No existence of a perfect cuboid endpoint is assumed.


2. Generic finite-fiber transfer theorem (NEW explicit cross-host result)
LEMMA 229BS.1. Let S_B be any finite family, and f,g:S_B->integers be single-valued maps. Suppose for some eta(B)->0, every fiber of each map on S_B has size <=B^eta(B). Write T_f=f(S_B) and T_g=g(S_B). Then
  |S_B|/B^eta(B) <= |T_f|, |T_g| <= |S_B|,              (229BS.1)
and
  B^(-eta(B)) |T_f| <= |T_g| <= B^eta(B) |T_f|.        (229BS.2)
PROOF: partition S_B into the disjoint nonempty fibers of f, and separately of g. Each fiber has size between 1 and B^eta. Summing gives (229BS.1), then eliminate |S_B|. Empty S_B gives |T_f|=|T_g|=0 and the same inequalities.
COROLLARY 229BS.2. At a fixed target exponent alpha>0, existence of epsilon>0 with |T_f|=O(B^(alpha-epsilon)) is equivalent to existence of epsilon'>0 with |T_g|=O(B^(alpha-epsilon')). In either direction one may take epsilon'=epsilon/2 for sufficiently large B.
CAUTION: a mere o(B^alpha) estimate without a fixed-power margin need NOT transfer through a B^o factor; neither does a polynomial height bound imply an occupied-value bound.


3. Apply to current rho and sigma
Set T_rho={rho(P):P in S_B(delta)} and T_sigma={sigma(P):P in S_B(delta)}. By 229BR their fibers are uniformly B^o on the whole physical population and hence on S_B(delta).
Therefore
  B^(-o(1)) |T_rho| <= |T_sigma| <= B^o(1)|T_rho|.     (229BS.3)
A fixed-power one-third support saving for T_rho holds IF AND ONLY IF one for T_sigma holds (possibly at a smaller saving exponent). This equivalence is a mathematical reduction, NOT a proof that either bound actually holds. There is no exact ordering |T_rho|<=|T_sigma| or reverse, nor any independence or multiplicative saving.
The two preferred receivers can therefore be treated as a single power-saving proof obligation with different available arithmetic information; proving the gate for either is enough.


4. Further degree-one radical receivers
Let u(P)=rad(e(P)), v(P)=rad(R(P)). Both are positive squarefree and <=B.
Retain the 229BR fixed-edge lemma: for every e<=B, the two factorizations (U-x)(U+x)=e^2 and (V-y)(V+y)=e^2 give at most O(tau(e^2)^2)=B^o physical endpoints at fixed e.
Retain the 229BR fixed-R lemma: e^2+z^2=R^2 allows B^o choices of (e,z) at fixed R; the fixed-edge lemma gives B^o further physical endpoints. Thus every R<=B has a uniform B^o fiber.
Fix u=r<=B. Every possible e<=B with rad(e)=r uses only prime divisors of r; 229BQ's UNIFORM polynomial-size prescribed-support Rankin lemma gives at most B^o possible e. Multiply by the fixed-e fiber B^o. Thus fixed u=rad(e) has B^o physical endpoints.
Likewise fixed v=s<=B allows only B^o positive R<=B supported on primes of s; multiply by the fixed-R physical fiber B^o. Thus fixed v=rad(R) has B^o endpoints.
Consequently the realized images of rho, sigma, e, R, rad(e), and rad(R), all restricted to the SAME S_B(delta), have cardinalities pairwise comparable up to B^o factors and have EQUIVALENT fixed-power one-third support gates.
This proves that even LINEAR-height SQUAREFREE scalars with uniform B^o physical fibers already exist. Further reduction of ambient receiver height without new selector-sensitive occupied-value information cannot, by itself, improve the M3 power exponent.


5. Exactly why the degree-one radicals are weaker as selectors
Let H=c12*c21 as in 229BR, G0=abH. By 229AD the six buckets h,d0,a,b,c12,c21 are pairwise coprime. Since gcd(e,R)=h, ab|e and gcd(ab,h)=1, we have
  gcd(ab,R)=1.                                        (229BS.4)
Since H|R, gcd(H,h)=1, and gcd(e,R)=h, we have
  gcd(H,e)=1.                                         (229BS.5)
With gcd(ab,H)=1, squarefree-kernel (odd-exponent) multiplicativity gives
  sf(G0)=sf(ab)*sf(H).                                (229BS.6)
Thus
  sf(G0)|rad(e)  iff sf(H)=1 (iff H is a square),      (229BS.7)
  sf(G0)|rad(R)  iff sf(ab)=1 (iff ab is a square).    (229BS.8)
Here sf means the original squarefree kernel, NOT the full prime radical. This distinction is essential: H>1 or ab>1 alone does not disprove divisibility when that factor is a perfect square.
In general neither degree-one radical u nor v retains the original source threshold as a standalone condition, whereas both 229BR rho and sigma satisfy sf(G0)|rho,sigma. Therefore the degree-one radical support-count contracts MUST keep the original physical source qualifier sf(G0)>B^(1/3-delta); replacing it by u>threshold or v>threshold is INVALID. No unconditional failure/existence assertion about any special H or ab stratum is made.


6. Operational theorem contract after 229BS
Keep the preferred source S_B(delta), alpha=1/3, and same selector conditions. Define T_f(B,delta)=f(S_B(delta)) for f in {rho,sigma,rad(e),rad(R)}.
An actual theorem |T_f|<<B^(1/3-epsilon) for ANY ONE of these for fixed epsilon>0 would imply |S_B(delta)|<<B^(1/3-epsilon/2) for sufficiently large B, and hence close the P_large tail. Conversely such a fixed-power bound for the P_large source implies a fixed-power bound for ALL four images; thus no simpler host automatically gives a new analytic input.
Priority stays with rho/sigma, because their squarefree radicals visibly contain sf(G0), unlike rad(e)/rad(R) in general. The new result REMOVES duplication in receiver-height optimization but supplies NO counting estimate.
Do not multiply T_rho and T_sigma as independent sieve events. Do not claim B^o equivalence transfers an arbitrary little-o bound. Do not treat rad(e) or rad(R) as a threshold-loss-free selector, except under the exact square conditions (229BS.7)-(229BS.8). Do not relabel these host equivalences as M3-T11-230 or as a resolved theorem gate.


7. State and dependencies

﻿Stage37-NEW-INPUT-DELTA-AUDIT-229BR — five-halves height same-radical refinement and quadratic edge-outer radical receiver
STATUS: POST_229BQ_SAME_SCALAR_HEIGHT_B_5_OVER_2_PROVED / QUADRATIC_EDGE_OUTER_RADICAL_RECEIVER_PROVED / UNIFORM_FIXED_SIGMA_B_O1_PHYSICAL_FIBER / FIXED_PHYSICAL_EDGE_AND_HEIGHT_FIBER_DIRECT_RECONSTRUCTION / NO_REALIZED_SUPPORT_POWER_SAVING / GLOBAL_CREDIT_0 / NO_REOPEN

1. Retained physical notation and statement
Take exactly the positive primitive canonical Stage37 physical endpoints P of 229AD/229BI/229BO/229BP/229BQ, with R(P)<=B and all original selector equations. Write
 e=gab, x=d0bc=d0 b c21 X, y=d0af=d0 a c12 Y, z=d0q,

 e^2+x^2=U^2, e^2+y^2=V^2, x^2+y^2=z^2, e^2+z^2=R^2,
 h=gcd(e,R)=gcd(g,q); c12=gcd(y,R)=gcd(n1,f), c21=gcd(x,R)=gcd(n2,c);
 G0=gcd(eR,xy)=ab c12 c21; E=g/h; X=c/c21; Y=f/c12.
Let H=c12*c21, m=min(X,Y), Phi=G0 E^2 m^2 and rho=rad(Phi)=rad(ab E H m).
Retain 229AD exact PAIRWISE coprimality of h,d0,a,b,c12,c21 and 229BQ uniform fixed-rho physical fiber B^{o(1)}.
NEW A: the SAME scalar rho from229BQ obeys
  0<rho<= R^(5/2) / (2sqrt(2) h^(3/2) d0 sqrt(ab)) <= B^(5/2)/(2sqrt(2)).    (229BR.1)
This improves the unconditional exponent 3 in229BQ to 5/2 WITHOUT changing the realized scalar or its fixed-value multiplicity.
NEW B: define a distinct positive squarefree scalar
  sigma(P):=rad(e(P)*R(P)).                                    (229BR.2)
Then 0<sigma<=eR<R^2<=B^2, sf(G0)|sigma, and uniformly for every realized integer s
  #{P:R(P)<=B, sigma(P)=s}=B^{o(1)}.                          (229BR.3)
The source implication sf(G0)>B^(1/3-delta) => sigma>B^(1/3-delta) is exact; the converse is not asserted.
2. Proof of SAME-scalar five-halves bound
By retained 229AD/229BI definitions, h|R, c12|R, c21|R. These three integers are pairwise coprime; therefore
  h*H = h*c12*c21 | R, hence H<=R/h.                          (229BR.4)
Since X,Y are positive and both >=m, the primitive missing-face relation gives
  q^2=(b c21 X)^2+(a c12 Y)^2
     >=m^2[(b c21)^2+(a c12)^2]
     >=2ab H m^2.                                           (229BR.5)
Here the final step is AM-GM; its two nonnegative summands have geometric mean ab c12 c21=abH.
Consequently m<=q/sqrt(2abH). Using rad(n)<=n,
  rho=rad(ab E H m)<=ab E H m
     <=(g q/h) sqrt(ab H/2)
     =(e q/h) sqrt(H/(2ab)).                                (229BR.6)

  A_x:=b c21 X,
  C_y:=a c12.                                    (229BO.6)
Then the primitive missing-face equation is
  A_x^2+(C_y Y)^2=q^2.                           (229BO.7)


The symmetric orientation uses
  A_y:=a c12 Y,
  C_x:=b c21,
with
  A_y^2+(C_x X)^2=q^2.                           (229BO.8)


3. Fixed (G0,Kx) has B^o(1) physical fiber


Fix a realized pair
  (G0,Kx)
on positive primitive Stage37 endpoints with R<=B.


Step 1 — split G0.
Every physical preimage gives an ordered factorization
  G0=a b c12 c21.
The number of ordered positive quadruple factorizations is
  <=tau_4(G0)=B^o(1),                            (229BO.9)
uniformly since G0<=B^2 on the physical locus.
All coprimality and selector conditions only remove candidates.


Step 2 — split Kx.
For a fixed quadruple above, every preimage has
  Kx=E X.
Hence there are at most
  tau(Kx)=B^o(1)                                 (229BO.10)
ordered choices (E,X).
Because Kx=H1/b^2 and H1=ex/G1<=B^2, Kx<=B^2 on the physical locus.


Step 3 — recover Y and q by one factorization.
Now A_x=b c21 X and C_y=a c12 are fixed.
Equation (229BO.7) gives
  (q-C_y Y)(q+C_y Y)=A_x^2.                      (229BO.11)


Thus every positive solution (Y,q) determines an ordered factor pair of A_x^2.
Consequently
  #{(Y,q)} <= tau(A_x^2)=B^o(1).                 (229BO.12)


Parity, positivity, divisibility by C_y, primitivity and physical conditions only remove factor pairs.


Step 4 — recover h.
Retain
  h=gcd(g,q), g=hE.
Therefore every physical h satisfies h|q and
  gcd(E,q/h)=1.
In particular
  #{h}<=tau(q)=B^o(1).                            (229BO.13)


Once h is chosen,
  g=hE,
  e=hEab                                          (229BO.14)
are fixed.


Step 5 — recover d0 and R by a second factorization.
The outer face equation is
  e^2+(d0 q)^2=R^2.
Hence
  (R-d0 q)(R+d0 q)=e^2.                          (229BO.15)


For fixed e,q, positive physical solutions (d0,R) inject into factor pairs of e^2, so
  #{(d0,R)}<=tau(e^2)=B^o(1).                    (229BO.16)


The exact cutoff R<=B only removes candidates.


Step 6 — finish the endpoint.
For each surviving tuple,
  x=d0 A_x,
  y=d0 C_y Y,
  z=d0 q                                          (229BO.17)
are fixed.
Then
  U^2=e^2+x^2,
  V^2=e^2+y^2                                    (229BO.18)
give at most one positive U,V; nonintegral cases are discarded.
All remaining canonical/primitive/selector checks are deterministic filters.


Multiplying the fixed number of divisor-function losses gives
  # {P:R(P)<=B, (G0(P),Kx(P))=(G,K)}
    =B^o(1)                                      (229BO.19)
uniformly for realized (G,K).


RESULT_229BO_G0_KX_TWO_COORDINATE_UNIFORM_PHYSICAL_FIBER=B_O1_PROVED_EXACT.


4. Symmetric fixed (G0,Ky) theorem


Interchange the x/y roles in Section 3.


Fix
  Ky=E Y.
After splitting
  G0=a b c12 c21
and
  Ky=E Y,
the leg
  A_y=a c12 Y
is fixed, and
  (q-b c21 X)(q+b c21 X)=A_y^2.                 (229BO.20)


This gives B^o(1) choices for (X,q), then h|q gives B^o(1), and
  (R-d0 q)(R+d0 q)=e^2
gives B^o(1) choices for (d0,R). The endpoint is then forced/check-only.


Therefore
  # {P:R(P)<=B, (G0(P),Ky(P))=(G,K)}
    =B^o(1)                                      (229BO.21)
uniformly.


RESULT_229BO_G0_KY_TWO_COORDINATE_UNIFORM_PHYSICAL_FIBER=B_O1_PROVED_EXACT.


5. Squareclass-preserving one-scalar compression


Define
  Theta_x:=G0 Kx^2,
  Theta_y:=G0 Ky^2.                              (229BO.22)


Because Kx^2 and Ky^2 are exact integer squares,
  sf(Theta_x)=sf(G0),
  sf(Theta_y)=sf(G0)                              (229BO.23)
exactly, including the 2-adic squarefree bit.


This is stronger than a radical-divisibility implication: the current squarefree kernel itself is unchanged.


Physical height is polynomial:
  G0<=B^2,
  Kx<=B^2,
  Ky<=B^2,
so
  Theta_x,Theta_y<=B^6.                           (229BO.24)


No claim is made that B^6 is sharp.


6. Fixed Theta_x has B^o(1) physical fiber


Fix a realized scalar value
  theta=Theta_x(P).


Every preimage supplies a divisor
  G0|theta
such that
  theta/G0=Kx^2
is a positive square.


The number of possible G0 is at most
  tau(theta)=B^o(1),                              (229BO.25)
because theta<=B^6 on the physical locus.
For each admissible G0, Kx is uniquely
  Kx=sqrt(theta/G0).


Section 3 then gives B^o(1) physical endpoints for fixed (G0,Kx).


Therefore
  # {P:R(P)<=B, Theta_x(P)=theta}
    =B^o(1)                                      (229BO.26)
uniformly for realized theta.


Identically,
  # {P:R(P)<=B, Theta_y(P)=theta}
    =B^o(1).                                     (229BO.27)


RESULT_229BO_THETA_X_FIXED_VALUE_UNIFORM_PHYSICAL_FIBER=B_O1_PROVED_EXACT.
RESULT_229BO_THETA_Y_FIXED_VALUE_UNIFORM_PHYSICAL_FIBER=B_O1_PROVED_EXACT.


7. Exact large-radical scalar pushforward


For fixed delta>0 define the current large-radical endpoint set
  P_large(B;delta)
   ={P:R(P)<=B,
       sf(G0(P))>B^(1/3-delta)}.                 (229BO.28)


Define the realized Theta_x value set
  T_x(B;delta)
   ={Theta_x(P):P in P_large(B;delta)}.           (229BO.29)


By (229BO.23),
  theta in T_x(B;delta)
  => sf(theta)>B^(1/3-delta),                    (229BO.30)
with exact equality of squarefree kernels endpoint-by-endpoint.


By the fixed-value fiber theorem (229BO.26),
  #P_large(B;delta)
    <= B^o(1) #T_x(B;delta).                     (229BO.31)


Thus any fixed-power realized-value estimate
  #T_x(B;delta) << B^(1/3-epsilon)               (229BO.32)
for some fixed epsilon>0 closes the current large-radical gate.


The same statement holds with T_y.


RESULT_229BO_EXACT_LARGE_RADICAL_ONE_SCALAR_PUSHFORWARD=PROVED_EXACT.


8. Comparison with the current scalar and support receivers


229AR:
  W_-=UV-eR
    =2^epsilon G0 r_-^2,
  W_-=O(B^2),
and the odd squarefree kernel equals that of G0.
Strength: low scalar height and no one-third threshold loss.
Remaining issue: no uniform B^o(1) fixed-W_- physical fiber has been proved.


229BN:
  Xi=(G0,H0,H1,H2)
with uniform B^o(1) fibers.
Strength: source reconstruction solved.
Remaining issue: four-coordinate occupied-support count.


229BO:
  Theta_x=G0 Kx^2
or symmetrically Theta_y=G0 Ky^2,
with
  sf(Theta)=sf(G0)
and uniform B^o(1) fixed-value physical fibers.
Strength: one scalar + exact squareclass preservation + solved source multiplicity.
Cost: only the coarse polynomial bound Theta<=B^6 is presently certified.


Therefore 229BO supplies a new theorem-facing interface not present in229AR or229BN.


9. Current theorem interface


NEW_CURRENT_PREFERRED_SUPPORT_INTERFACE:
SQUARECLASS_PRESERVING_ONE_SCALAR_OCCUPIED_VALUE.


Preferred scalar:
  Theta_x=G0 (E X)^2.
Symmetric scalar:
  Theta_y=G0 (E Y)^2.


Exact properties:
- positive integer scalar on every physical endpoint;
- Theta<=B^6;
- sf(Theta)=sf(G0);
- every fixed realized Theta fiber is B^o(1).


Sufficient new input:
for some fixed delta,epsilon>0,
  #{theta realized as Theta_x(P), R(P)<=B,
      sf(theta)>B^(1/3-delta)}
    << B^(1/3-epsilon).                           (229BO.33)


Parallel retained interfaces:
(A)229AR low-height W_- scalar with unresolved fixed-value fiber;
(B)229BN four-coordinate support;
(C)229BM hard-remainder packet-square occupancy;
(D)229BF outer-floor removal;
(E)selector-conditioned squarefree-modulus radical sieve.


CURRENT_BLOCKER:
NO_FIXED_POWER_BOUND_FOR_REALIZED_SQUARECLASS_PRESERVING_THETA_X_SCALAR_VALUES_WITH_LARGE_SF_AT_ONE_THIRD_BUDGET.


10. Firewalls


DO NOT:
- count arbitrary integers theta<=B^6 with large sf(theta) and call that a physical support bound;
- infer sparsity from sf(Theta)=sf(G0) alone;
- infer a fixed-power bound from B^o(1) fibers alone;
- identify the new Theta scalar with229AR W_-; they are different receivers with different height/fiber tradeoffs;
- multiply the x- and y-oriented scalar conditions as independent events; every physical endpoint deterministically carries both;
- drop exact primitive/canonical/selector conditions in a theorem transfer;
- change authority, credit, gate, closure, production HOLD, or P/M3 status from this support compression alone.


11. State


No endpoint count with a new fixed-power saving is proved.
No perfect-cuboid existence/nonexistence conclusion is claimed.

12. Dependencies


Load-bearing retained inputs:

The new fiber bounds use only exact integer factorization:
  (q-CY)(q+CY)=A^2
and

records.content:
﻿Stage37-NEW-INPUT-DELTA-AUDIT-229BN — dual macro-cofactor triangle and four-coordinate support compression


STATUS: POST_229BM_DUAL_MACRO_COFACTOR_TRIANGLE / PROVED_EXACT_THREE_PRIMITIVE_MACRO_LEG_COFACTORS / PROVED_PAIRWISE_GCD_RECOVERY_OF_RESIDUAL_EDGE_CORES / PROVED_EXACT_SQUARE_DIAGONAL_RECOVERY_OF_a_b_d0 / PROVED_SYMMETRIC_CENTRAL_ROOT_CLUSTER_DUAL_TRIANGLE / PROVED_FOUR_COORDINATE_SUPPORT_UNIFORM_B_O1_PHYSICAL_FIBER / WHOLE_POPULATION_SUPPORT_COMPRESSION / NO_COUNTING_PROMOTION / GLOBAL_CREDIT=0 / NO_GLOBAL_REOPEN


TYPE: POST-229BM DUAL CONTENT-COFACTOR TRIANGLE / LOWER-DIMENSIONAL EXACT SUPPORT PUSHFORWARD / DIVISOR-BOUNDED PHYSICAL RECONSTRUCTION / 229AX SUPPORT COMPRESSION


OPERATIONAL_AUTHORITY: M3-T11-229
LATEST_MATHEMATICAL_CONSTRUCTION: M3-T11-228
PREVIOUS_POST_229_DELTA: Stage37-NEW-INPUT-DELTA-AUDIT-229BM
PRIMARY_GATE: M3-T11-GATE-001 OPEN
M3_T11_230: NOT ISSUED
GLOBAL_COUNTING_CREDIT: 0
CARD_DOC_ID: 1iTdnGyt3GY_C4nfJ8nrwT94VGc3BsAzLlSNIjzU93dI


1. Scope


229BI proved the exact macro-content triangle
  G0=gcd(eR,xy)=C+ C-,
  G1=gcd(yR,ex)=C- C0,
  G2=gcd(xR,ey)=C+ C0,
with
  C0=h d0,
  C+=b c12,
  C-=a c21,
and pairwise-coprime six physical content buckets
  h,d0,a,b,c12,c21.


229BM then completed the three symmetric central packet-square charts.


This card studies the complementary primitive macro-leg cofactors
  H0:=xy/G0,
  H1:=ex/G1,
  H2:=ey/G2.                                      (229BN.1)


The main result is that H0,H1,H2 themselves form a second exact triangle, dual to the 229BI content triangle. Their pairwise gcds recover three residual edge cores exactly, and their diagonal quotients recover a,b,d0 as exact positive square roots.


As a consequence, the whole physical endpoint population admits the four-coordinate support map
  Xi(P)=(G0,H0,H1,H2)
with uniformly B^o(1) physical fibers at exact height R<=B.


This is a whole-population support compression. It does not require the 229BL hard-remainder restriction.


2. Retained nested factorization and residual cores


Retain 229AD:
  e = g a b,
  x = d0 b c,
  y = d0 a f,                                    (229BN.2)
with
  gcd(a,b)=1,
  gcd(c,f)=1,
  gcd(g,d0)=1,
  gcd(g,c)=gcd(g,f)=1,
  gcd(a,d0)=gcd(a,c)=1,
  gcd(b,d0)=gcd(b,f)=1.


Retain
  h=gcd(g,q),
  c12|f,
  c21|c,
where
  (bc)^2+(af)^2=q^2,
  z=d0 q.                                        (229BN.3)


Define positive residual cores
  E:=g/h,
  X:=c/c21,
  Y:=f/c12.                                      (229BN.4)


From the retained gcd relations,
  gcd(E,X)=gcd(E,Y)=gcd(X,Y)=1.                  (229BN.5)


Indeed E|g, X|c, Y|f and 229AD gives gcd(g,c)=gcd(g,f)=gcd(c,f)=1.


RESULT_229BN_RESIDUAL_EDGE_CORES_PAIRWISE_COPRIME=PROVED_EXACT.


3. Exact dual macro-cofactor factorization


Retain 229BI:
  G0=a b c12 c21,
  G1=a c21 h d0,
  G2=b c12 h d0.                                 (229BN.6)


Substitute (229BN.2)-(229BN.4) into (229BN.1).


For H0:
  H0
   = xy/G0
   = (d0 b c)(d0 a f)/(a b c12 c21)
   = d0^2 (c/c21)(f/c12)
   = d0^2 X Y.                                   (229BN.7)


For H1:
  H1
   = ex/G1
   = (g a b)(d0 b c)/(a c21 h d0)
   = b^2 (g/h)(c/c21)
   = b^2 E X.                                    (229BN.8)


For H2:
  H2
   = ey/G2
   = (g a b)(d0 a f)/(b c12 h d0)
   = a^2 (g/h)(f/c12)
   = a^2 E Y.                                    (229BN.9)


Therefore
  H0 H1 H2 = (a b d0 E X Y)^2.                  (229BN.10)


So the three primitive macro-leg cofactors have exact square product, independently of the already-known square product G0G1G2.


RESULT_229BN_DUAL_MACRO_COFACTOR_TRIANGLE=PROVED_EXACT.
RESULT_229BN_H0_H1_H2_PRODUCT_IS_EXACT_SQUARE=PROVED_EXACT.


4. Pairwise gcds recover the residual cores exactly


Using (229BN.7)-(229BN.9),


  gcd(H0,H1)
   = X gcd(d0^2 Y, b^2 E).


The remaining gcd is 1 because
  gcd(d0,b)=1,
  gcd(d0,E)=1 from E|g and gcd(g,d0)=1,
  gcd(Y,b)=1 from Y|f and gcd(b,f)=1,
  gcd(Y,E)=1 from Y|f,E|g and gcd(g,f)=1.


Hence
  gcd(H0,H1)=X.                                   (229BN.11)


Similarly,
  gcd(H0,H2)=Y                                    (229BN.12)
using gcd(d0,a)=gcd(d0,E)=gcd(X,a)=gcd(X,E)=1,


and
  gcd(H1,H2)=E                                    (229BN.13)
using gcd(a,b)=gcd(b,Y)=gcd(X,a)=gcd(X,Y)=1.


By (229BN.5),
  gcd(H0,H1,H2)=1.                                (229BN.14)


Thus the dual cofactor triangle has pairwise gcd colors
  H0∩H1 : X,
  H0∩H2 : Y,
  H1∩H2 : E,
with empty common prime support across all three.


RESULT_229BN_DUAL_TRIANGLE_PAIRWISE_GCD_RECOVERY=PROVED_EXACT.
RESULT_229BN_DUAL_TRIANGLE_TRIPLE_GCD_ONE=PROVED_EXACT.


5. Exact recovery of a,b,d0 from the cofactor triangle


Equations (229BN.7)-(229BN.13) imply


  X = gcd(H0,H1),
  Y = gcd(H0,H2),
  E = gcd(H1,H2).                                 (229BN.15)


Then
  d0^2 = H0/(XY),
  b^2  = H1/(EX),
  a^2  = H2/(EY).                                 (229BN.16)


All three right-hand sides are exact positive integer squares on realized physical support, so


  d0 = sqrt(H0/(XY)),
  b  = sqrt(H1/(EX)),
  a  = sqrt(H2/(EY))                              (229BN.17)


are uniquely recovered.


Therefore the realized cofactor triple (H0,H1,H2) determines exactly
  (a,b,d0,E,X,Y).                                 (229BN.18)


This is stronger than merely knowing that H0H1H2 is a square.


RESULT_229BN_COFACTOR_TRIPLE_RECOVERS_SIX_EDGE_PARAMETERS=PROVED_EXACT.


6. Symmetric central-root cluster crosswalk


For chart j=0,1,2 let T_j denote the transverse macro leg:
  T0=xy,
  T1=ex,
  T2=ey,
so
  Hj=T_j/Gj.


Retain the 229BM four central forms
  lambda_j,Sigma_j,M_j,N_j
with
  lambda_j Sigma_j=2(P_j-L_j),
  M_j N_j=2(P_j+L_j).


Multiplying,
  lambda_j Sigma_j M_j N_j
   =4(P_j^2-L_j^2)
   =4 T_j^2.                                      (229BN.19)


Write the odd packet-square forms from 229BM as
  O(lambda_j)=Q_j^- (u_j^-)^2,
  O(Sigma_j) =Q_j^+ (u_j^+)^2,
  O(M_j)     =P_j^- (v_j^-)^2,
  O(N_j)     =P_j^+ (v_j^+)^2,
with
  Q_j^-Q_j^+=P_j^-P_j^+=(Gj)_odd.


Taking odd parts in (229BN.19), all quantities positive, gives
  u_j^- u_j^+ v_j^- v_j^+
    = O(T_j/G_j)
    = O(Hj).                                      (229BN.20)


For j=0 this is retained 229AV.14. For j=1,2 it is the exact symmetric extension.


Define
  rho_j:=u_j^- u_j^+ v_j^- v_j^+=O(Hj).           (229BN.21)


Then (229BN.11)-(229BN.13) imply
  gcd(rho_0,rho_1)=O(X),
  gcd(rho_0,rho_2)=O(Y),
  gcd(rho_1,rho_2)=O(E),                          (229BN.22)
and
  rho_0 rho_1 rho_2
is an exact odd square.                               (229BN.23)


Thus the three complete central-root clusters form the odd part of the dual cofactor triangle.


RESULT_229BN_SYMMETRIC_CENTRAL_ROOT_CLUSTER_DUAL_TRIANGLE=PROVED_EXACT.


7. Four-coordinate whole-population support map


Define on positive primitive Stage37 physical endpoints with R<=B


  Xi(P):=(G0,H0,H1,H2).                            (229BN.24)


Let Xi_B be the realized image.


All four coordinates have polynomial physical height:
  G0<=min(eR,xy)<=B^2,
  H0=xy/G0<=B^2,
  H1=ex/G1<=B^2,
  H2=ey/G2<=B^2.                                  (229BN.25)


Fix one realized tuple
  xi=(G0,H0,H1,H2).


By Sections 4-5, the triple H0,H1,H2 uniquely recovers
  X,Y,E,d0,b,a.                                   (229BN.26)


From retained (229BN.6),
  Cprod:=G0/(ab)=c12 c21.                         (229BN.27)


Hence the ordered pair (c12,c21) has at most
  tau(Cprod)
possibilities.


For each divisor choice c12|Cprod, set
  c21=Cprod/c12,
  c=c21 X,
  f=c12 Y.                                       (229BN.28)


Then the retained primitive missing-face equation forces
  q^2=(bc)^2+(af)^2.                              (229BN.29)


For the chosen split there is therefore at most one positive q. If the right side is not a square, that split has no physical preimage.


When q exists, retain
  h=gcd(g,q),
  g=hE.
Therefore necessarily h|q. Thus h has at most
  tau(q)
choices. The exact condition gcd(hE,q)=h only removes divisor choices.


Once h is fixed,
  g=hE,
  e=gab,
  x=d0 b c,
  y=d0 a f,
  z=d0 q                                          (229BN.30)
are uniquely fixed.


Then
  R^2=e^2+z^2,
  U^2=e^2+x^2,
  V^2=e^2+y^2                                    (229BN.31)
give at most one positive R,U,V each, with nonintegral candidates discarded.


Therefore
  # Xi^{-1}(xi)
   <= sum_{c12|Cprod} tau(q(c12))
   <= tau(Cprod) max_{c12|Cprod} tau(q(c12)).      (229BN.32)


On physical endpoints,
  Cprod<=G0<=B^2,
  q=z/d0<=z<R<=B.
The standard uniform divisor bound gives


  # Xi^{-1}(xi)=B^o(1)                            (229BN.33)


uniformly for realized xi.


RESULT_229BN_FOUR_COORDINATE_SUPPORT_UNIFORM_PHYSICAL_FIBER=B_O1_PROVED_EXACT.


8. Large-radical gate pushforward


Let
  P_large(B;delta)
be the current exact positive primitive Stage37 endpoint population satisfying
  R<=B,
  sf(G0)>B^(1/3-delta).


Let
  Xi_B^large(delta)
   :={xi in Xi_B : sf(G0)>B^(1/3-delta)}.          (229BN.34)


By (229BN.33),


  #P_large(B;delta)
   <= B^o(1) #Xi_B^large(delta).                   (229BN.35)


Thus a fixed-power support estimate
  #Xi_B^large(delta) << B^(1/3-epsilon)            (229BN.36)
for some fixed epsilon>0 is sufficient for the current large-radical gate after absorbing the B^o(1) fiber.


This is a genuine lower-coordinate occupied-support contract. It replaces the source-reconstruction issue by a count of a realized four-coordinate arithmetic image.


229AX had already proved a B^o(1) fiber for a seven-coordinate e-base atom/root support after rank-one redundancy. 229BN gives a different, symmetric four-coordinate support using the three macro contents/cofactors. No claim is made that the four-coordinate image is already small.


RESULT_229BN_LARGE_RADICAL_FOUR_COORDINATE_SUPPORT_PUSHFORWARD=PROVED_EXACT.


9. Current theorem interface


NEW_CURRENT_PREFERRED_SUPPORT_INTERFACE:
FOUR_COORDINATE_MACRO_CONTENT_COFACTOR_OCCUPIED_SUPPORT.


Target the realized set
  Xi_B={(G0,H0,H1,H2)}
with:
- exact physical origin and exact R<=B cutoff;
- G0=gcd(eR,xy);
- H0=xy/G0, H1=ex/G1, H2=ey/G2;
- exact dual triangle
    gcd(H0,H1)=X,
    gcd(H0,H2)=Y,
    gcd(H1,H2)=E,
    H0H1H2=square;
- current gate
    sf(G0)>B^(1/3-delta).


Sufficient new counting input:
  #Xi_B^large(delta) << B^(1/3-epsilon)

229BL completed the three positive central-gap divisor charts
  lambda_e(2e+lambda_e)=2(R-U)(R-V),
  lambda_y(2y+lambda_y)=2(R-z)(R-V),
  lambda_x(2x+lambda_x)=2(R-z)(R-U),
and localized the unresolved population, at an o(B^(1/3)) same-physical cost, to the sector where all three outer-gap pair products exceed T=B^(1/3-eta).


229AU and 229AV had previously proved an exact raw-packet-times-square normalization and complete central K4 odd-gcd graph only for the e-base central chart. The y-base and x-base central charts did not yet exist at that point.


This card proves that the 229AU/229AV normalization is permutation-invariant and therefore extends exactly to the two new 229BL charts. It then combines that full symmetric normalization with the 229BL hard remainder. The result is a stronger theorem interface: the six low central divisor factors on the hard remainder are not merely constrained by one fixed squareclass product; each factor individually is a finite 2-adic bit times an exact raw-content gcd packet times a square, and the paired factors are quantitatively off diagonal.


No global endpoint count follows from this structural refinement alone.


2. Uniform three-chart notation


For j=0,1,2 define edge triples, adjacent face diagonals, macro legs, macro hypotenuse products and contents by


j=0:
  q0=e, r0=x, s0=y,
  A0=U, B0=V,
  L0=eR, T0=xy, P0=UV,
  G0=gcd(eR,xy).


j=1:
  q1=y, r1=x, s1=e,
  A1=z, B1=V,
  L1=yR, T1=ex, P1=zV,
  G1=gcd(yR,ex).


j=2:
  q2=x, r2=y, s2=e,
  A2=z, B2=U,
  L2=xR, T2=ey, P2=zU,
  G2=gcd(xR,ey).


Then, exactly,
  L_j^2+T_j^2=P_j^2,
and 229BI gives
  G0=C+ C-,
  G1=C- C0,
  G2=C+ C0,
with C0,C+,C- pairwise coprime and G0G1G2 a square.


For each j define four positive central linear forms
  lambda_j := A_j+B_j-R-q_j,
  Sigma_j  := q_j+A_j+B_j+R,
  M_j      := q_j+A_j+B_j-R,
  N_j      := R+A_j+B_j-q_j.                       (229BM.1)


Thus
  lambda_0=lambda_e, M_0=e+U+V-R,
  lambda_1=lambda_y, M_1=y+z+V-R,
  lambda_2=lambda_x, M_2=x+z+U-R.


The exact identities are
  lambda_j Sigma_j = 2(P_j-L_j),                   (229BM.2)
  M_j N_j           = 2(P_j+L_j),                 (229BM.3)
  lambda_j M_j      = 2(R-A_j)(R-B_j),            (229BM.4)
  M_j-lambda_j      = 2q_j.                       (229BM.5)


The first two are the minus/plus gap factorizations of the three macro Pythagorean triples. The third is the symmetric 229AQ/229BL central divisor chart.


RESULT_229BM_THREE_FOUR_FORM_CENTRAL_RECTANGLES=PROVED_EXACT.


3. Common-gcd nuisance for all three charts


Set
  d_j := gcd(r_j,s_j).
Then
  d_0=gcd(x,y)=d0,
  d_1=gcd(x,e)=b,
  d_2=gcd(y,e)=a.                                  (229BM.6)


The primitive physical edge triple gives
  gcd(q_j,d_j)=1.
Also if a prime divided d_j and R, then from
  R^2=q_j^2+r_j^2+s_j^2
it would divide q_j, a contradiction. Hence
  gcd(q_j R,d_j)=1.                                (229BM.7)


Let an odd prime power p^m divide both lambda_j and Sigma_j. From their sum and difference,
  p^m | A_j+B_j,
  p^m | R+q_j.
Therefore
  p^m | A_j^2-B_j^2 = r_j^2-s_j^2,
  p^m | R^2-q_j^2   = r_j^2+s_j^2.
Since p is odd,
  p^m | r_j^2 and p^m | s_j^2,
so
  gcd_odd(lambda_j,Sigma_j) | d_j^2.              (229BM.8)


The same proof using
  M_j+N_j=2(A_j+B_j),
  N_j-M_j=2(R-q_j)
gives
  gcd_odd(M_j,N_j) | d_j^2.                       (229BM.9)


By (229BM.7), both common-gcd nuisances are coprime to the macro leg L_j=q_jR.


For j=0 these are retained 229AS facts. For j=1,2 they are the new exact symmetric completions.


RESULT_229BM_THREE_CHART_COMMON_GCD_NUISANCE_FIREWALL=PROVED_EXACT.


4. Exact raw-content gcd matchings in every chart


Define odd gcd packets
  Q_j^- := gcd_odd(L_j,lambda_j),
  Q_j^+ := gcd_odd(L_j,Sigma_j),
  P_j^- := gcd_odd(L_j,M_j),
  P_j^+ := gcd_odd(L_j,N_j).                       (229BM.10)


Because the common gcds in (229BM.8)-(229BM.9) are coprime to L_j,
  gcd(Q_j^-,Q_j^+)=1,
  gcd(P_j^-,P_j^+)=1.                              (229BM.11)


Using (229BM.2),
  gcd(L_j,P_j-L_j)=gcd(L_j,P_j)=G_j
for the integral macro Pythagorean triple. Therefore
  Q_j^- Q_j^+ = (G_j)_odd.                         (229BM.12)


Similarly, using (229BM.3),
  P_j^- P_j^+ = (G_j)_odd.                         (229BM.13)


Hence every macro content G_j has two exact coprime raw-content matchings by positive O(B)-height central linear forms.


For j=0 this is retained 229AS. Equations (229BM.12)-(229BM.13) for j=1,2 are new symmetric exact matchings.


RESULT_229BM_THREE_MACRO_EXACT_COPRIME_RAW_G_MATCHINGS=PROVED_EXACT.


5. Individual packet-times-square normal forms


Let O(n) denote the odd part of n.


From the macro Pythagorean gap/content lemma applied to (229BM.2),
  O(lambda_j) O(Sigma_j)
is (G_j)_odd times a square.
Together with (229BM.12),
  [O(lambda_j)/Q_j^-] [O(Sigma_j)/Q_j^+]
is a square. Let h_Q,j be the common squarefree kernel of these two quotients. Any prime dividing h_Q,j divides both lambda_j and Sigma_j, so by (229BM.8)
  h_Q,j | rad(d_j).                                (229BM.14)


Likewise (229BM.3) and (229BM.13) give a squarefree h_P,j with
  h_P,j | rad(d_j).                                (229BM.15)


To compare the two nuisances, split the exact raw packets by the q_j and R sides:
  A_j^-:=gcd_odd(q_j,lambda_j),
  A_j^+:=gcd_odd(q_j,Sigma_j),
  C_j^-:=gcd_odd(R,lambda_j),
  C_j^+:=gcd_odd(R,Sigma_j).


The same additive rectangle used in 229AS gives the checkerboard
  Q_j^-=A_j^- C_j^-,
  Q_j^+=A_j^+ C_j^+,
  P_j^-=A_j^- C_j^+,
  P_j^+=A_j^+ C_j^-.                              (229BM.16)


The q-side product A_j^-A_j^+ is the odd product of the two q_j-side physical content buckets; the R-side product C_j^-C_j^+ is the odd product of the two R-side content buckets. This is the 229AD six-bucket decomposition under the edge permutation (q_j,r_j,s_j).

  sf_odd((R-A_j)(R-B_j))

Let T>=1. On the 229BL hard remainder require
  (R-U)(R-V)>T,
  (R-z)(R-V)>T,
  (R-z)(R-U)>T.                                   (229BM.21)

They factor through six positive O(B) linear forms:
  2J0=lambda_e S_e,
  2J1=lambda_y S_y,
  2J2=lambda_x S_x,                               (229BL.11)
where
  S_e:=e+U+V+R,
  S_y:=y+z+V+R,
  S_x:=x+z+U+R.                                   (229BL.12)


Every displayed factor is <4B on R<=B.


For T0=(eR,xy,UV), J0 is the retained A-leg gap and has exponent epsilon_0.
For T1=(ex,yR,zV), J1 is the complementary B-leg gap and therefore has exponent 1-epsilon_1.
For T2=(ey,xR,zU), J2 has exponent 1-epsilon_2.


Using229BK
  epsilon_0+epsilon_1+epsilon_2 even,
the mixed exponent
  epsilon_0+(1-epsilon_1)+(1-epsilon_2)
is even.


Since229BI proved
  G0G1G2=(C0 C+ C-)^2,
it follows that
  J0 J1 J2
is an exact positive integer square.                (229BL.13)


RESULT_229BL_THREE_LOW_HEIGHT_MACRO_GAPS_PRODUCT_SQUARE=PROVED_EXACT.


5. Six O(B) linear forms have fixed squareclass 2
Multiplying (229BL.11),
  lambda_e lambda_y lambda_x S_e S_y S_x
    =8 J0J1J2
    =2 * square.                                   (229BL.14)


Hence
  sf(lambda_e lambda_y lambda_x S_e S_y S_x)=2.   (229BL.15)


This is a fully global, low-height scalar relation: six positive O(B) linear forms derived from one physical endpoint have fixed squareclass exactly 2.


It is NOT an independent odd-prime sieve condition on top of229BI/BJ; its odd support is inherited from the same macro content triangle.


RESULT_229BL_SIX_LOW_HEIGHT_LINEAR_FORMS_FIXED_SQUARECLASS_2=PROVED_EXACT.


6. Second six-linear fixed-squareclass relation from the outer gaps
Set
  M_e:=2e+lambda_e=e+U+V-R,
  M_y:=2y+lambda_y=y+z+V-R,
  M_x:=2x+lambda_x=x+z+U-R.                       (229BL.16)


Multiplying the three first divisor charts (229BL.9),
  lambda_e lambda_y lambda_x M_e M_y M_x
   =8 (g_U g_V g_z)^2
   =2 * square.                                    (229BL.17)


Therefore
  sf(lambda_e lambda_y lambda_x M_e M_y M_x)=2.   (229BL.18)


Combining (229BL.15) and (229BL.18),
  (S_e S_y S_x)/(M_e M_y M_x)
is a rational square.                               (229BL.19)


RESULT_229BL_SECOND_SIX_LINEAR_FIXED_SQUARECLASS_2=PROVED_EXACT.
RESULT_229BL_LONG_SHORT_LINEAR_PRODUCT_RATIO_IS_RATIONAL_SQUARE=PROVED_EXACT.


No density saving is claimed from these identities alone.


7. Exact divisor encodings for all three outer-gap pair sectors
For the e-chart,229AQ already proved that fixed positive
  C=g_U, D=g_V, lambda=lambda_e
with lambda|2CD reconstruct
  e=(2CD/lambda-lambda)/2,
  U=e+D+lambda,
  V=e+C+lambda,
  R=e+C+D+lambda,
and then x,y,z are uniquely determined if they exist.


The identical argument applies to the two new charts.


For fixed
  C=g_z, D=g_V, lambda=lambda_y,
one reconstructs uniquely
  y=(2CD/lambda-lambda)/2,
  z=y+D+lambda,
  V=y+C+lambda,
  R=y+C+D+lambda,
then x,e,U if they exist.


For fixed
  C=g_z, D=g_U, lambda=lambda_x,
one reconstructs uniquely
  x=(2CD/lambda-lambda)/2,
  z=x+D+lambda,
  U=x+C+lambda,
  R=x+C+D+lambda,
then y,e,V if they exist.


Thus each endpoint injects into the corresponding labelled divisor triple (C,D,lambda).


RESULT_229BL_THREE_DIVISOR_CHARTS_HAVE_ENDPOINT_FIBER_AT_MOST_ONE=PROVED_EXACT.


8. Three small pair-product sectors have H^(1+o(1)) count
Define
  N_UV(H;B):=#{physical endpoints R<=B: g_U g_V<=H},
  N_zV(H;B):=#{physical endpoints R<=B: g_z g_V<=H},
  N_zU(H;B):=#{physical endpoints R<=B: g_z g_U<=H}.


For each chart, lambda is a positive divisor of 2CD. Therefore
  N_UV(H;B),
  N_zV(H;B),
  N_zU(H;B)
   <= sum_{CD<=H} tau(2CD)
   = H^(1+o(1)),                                  (229BL.20)
uniformly in B.


The first bound is retained229AQ; the latter two are new symmetric completions.


Hence their union also satisfies
  # {R<=B: min(g_U g_V,g_z g_V,g_z g_U)<=H}
    = H^(1+o(1)).                                 (229BL.21)


For any fixed eta>0, with
  H=B^(1/3-eta),
this is
  B^(1/3-eta+o(1))
  =o(B^(1/3)).                                    (229BL.22)


RESULT_229BL_THREE_SMALL_OUTER_PAIR_SECTORS_UNION_o_M3=PROVED_SCOPED.


9. Hard-remainder localization
At an o(B^(1/3)) same-physical cost, the current large-K gate may therefore be restricted simultaneously to

  (R-z)(R-V)>B^(1/3-eta),
  (R-z)(R-U)>B^(1/3-eta),                         (229BL.23)
for any fixed eta>0.


Equivalently all three pair products among
  g_U,g_V,g_z
are large.


Consequently
  g_U g_V g_z > B^(1/2-3eta/2).                  (229BL.24)


This is a genuine global localization of the remaining physical population, but not a closure theorem.


RESULT_229BL_HARD_REMAINDER_ALL_THREE_OUTER_PAIR_PRODUCTS_LARGE=PROVED_SCOPED.

10. Current theorem interface after229BL
CURRENT_PREFERRED_NEW_INTERNAL_INTERFACE:
THREE_CENTRAL_GAP_LOW_HEIGHT_OCCUPANCY.


Count physical endpoints satisfying simultaneously:

﻿Stage37-NEW-INPUT-DELTA-AUDIT-229BK — full 2-adic macro-gap squareclass closure and eight square-product identities


STATUS: POST_229BJ_FULL_MACRO_GAP_2ADIC_CLOSURE_COMPLETE / PROVED_PRIMITIVE_EDGE_PARITY_EXACTLY_ONE_ODD / PROVED_UNIQUE_EVEN_RAW_HILBERT_CONTENT_PACKET / PROVED_MACRO_GAP_EPSILON_SUM_EVEN / PROVED_ALL_EIGHT_SIGNED_MACRO_GAP_PRODUCTS_ARE_INTEGER_SQUARES / PROVED_FULL_SQUAREFREE_KERNEL_TRIANGLE_INCLUDING_2 / PROVED_W0_IS_STRICT_GLOBAL_MINIMUM_AND_W1_W2_ORDER_FOLLOWS_y_x / NEW_SCALAR_ONLY_GLOBAL_PACKET_INTERFACE / NO_COUNTING_PROMOTION / GLOBAL_CREDIT=0 / NO_GLOBAL_REOPEN
TYPE: POST-229BJ PARITY COMPLETION / THREE-MACRO-PYTHAGOREAN 2-ADIC SYNCHRONIZATION / GLOBAL INTEGER-SQUARE PRODUCT / FULL SQUAREFREE-PACKET TRIANGLE / ARCHIMEDEAN GAP ORDER
OPERATIONAL_AUTHORITY: M3-T11-229
LATEST_MATHEMATICAL_CONSTRUCTION: M3-T11-228
PREVIOUS_POST_229_DELTA: Stage37-NEW-INPUT-DELTA-AUDIT-229BJ
PRIMARY_GATE: M3-T11-GATE-001 OPEN
M3_T11_230: NOT ISSUED
GLOBAL_COUNTING_CREDIT: 0
CARD_DOC_ID: 1ijamDGsANEgNEaphsd5a_FdpgBSzMXYAMI3ORbsvEHE


1. Scope
229BI proved the exact odd-support/content triangle for the three macro Pythagorean triples
  T0: (eR, xy, UV),
  T1: (ex, yR, zV),
  T2: (ey, xR, zU),
with contents
  G0=C+ C-,
  G1=C- C0,
  G2=C+ C0,
where
  C0=h d0,
  C+=b c12,
  C-=a c21,
and G0 G1 G2=(C0 C+ C-)^2.


229BJ proved that the associated odd-prime node colors give no fixed-power local sieve improvement.


The remaining unresolved structural issue is the 2-adic part. The 229BI theorem was deliberately stated primarily on odd squarefree kernels because the three independent Pythagorean gap parity bits were not synchronized there.


This card synchronizes those bits using only primitive physical parity. The result is stronger than an odd-support statement: all eight products obtained by independently choosing the plus or minus Euclid gap in the three macro triples are exact positive integer squares.


2. Primitive physical parity: exactly one edge is odd
The primitive positive physical endpoint has
  gcd(e,x,y)=1
and the three face-square equations
  e^2+x^2=U^2,
  e^2+y^2=V^2,
  x^2+y^2=z^2.


No two of e,x,y can be odd, because the sum of two odd squares is 2 mod4 and cannot be a square.


They also cannot all be even by primitivity.


Therefore exactly one of
  e,x,y
is odd.                                                (229BK.1)


Then
  R^2=e^2+x^2+y^2
is odd, hence R is odd.


If the unique odd edge is e, then x,y are even and U,V,R are odd while z is even.
If the unique odd edge is x, then e,y are even and x,U,R are odd while V is even.
If the unique odd edge is y, then e,x are even and y,V,R are odd while U is even.


RESULT_229BK_EXACTLY_ONE_PHYSICAL_EDGE_ODD=PROVED.


3. Exactly one raw Hilbert content packet is even
Retain229AD:
  h|q with q odd,
  c12|n1 and c21|n2 with n1,n2 primitive Pythagorean hypotenuses.
Thus
  h,c12,c21
are all odd.


Hence the parities of
  C0=h d0,
  C+=b c12,
  C-=a c21
are exactly the parities of
  d0,b,a
respectively.


Using the physical gcd meanings:
  d0=gcd(x,y),
  b=gcd(e,x),
  a=gcd(e,y),
and (229BK.1):


- if e is odd, x,y are even, so d0 is even while a,b are odd:
    C0 even, C+ odd, C- odd;
- if x is odd, e,y are even, so a is even while d0,b are odd:
    C- even, C0 odd, C+ odd;
- if y is odd, e,x are even, so b is even while d0,a are odd:
    C+ even, C0 odd, C- odd.


Therefore exactly one of
  C0,C+,C-
is even.                                               (229BK.2)


Consequently exactly one of
  G0=C+C-,
  G1=C-C0,
  G2=C+C0
is odd: it is the product of the two odd C-packets, i.e. the macro content opposite the unique even packet.


RESULT_229BK_UNIQUE_EVEN_RAW_HILBERT_PACKET=PROVED_EXACT.
RESULT_229BK_EXACTLY_ONE_MACRO_CONTENT_ODD=PROVED_EXACT.


4. Macro Euclid-gap parity bits
For j=0,1,2 write the first two legs of Tj as
  (Aj,Bj):
  (A0,B0)=(eR,xy),
  (A1,B1)=(ex,yR),
  (A2,B2)=(ey,xR).


Normalize by the exact content Gj. Retain229AR's primitive Pythagorean gap lemma in the form:
there is epsilon_j in {0,1} such that
  Hj-Aj = 2^epsilon_j Gj (r_j^-)^2,
  Hj+Aj = 2^epsilon_j Gj (r_j^+)^2,               (229BK.3)
where Hj is UV,zV,zU respectively.


In the retained Euclid proof,
  epsilon_j=0 exactly when Aj/Gj is the even primitive leg,
  epsilon_j=1 exactly when Aj/Gj is the odd primitive leg.  (229BK.4)


Let
  E=v2(e), X=v2(x), Y=v2(y).
Since R is odd, v2(R)=0.


Case A: e odd.
Then E=0 and X,Y>0. Because x^2+y^2=z^2, X and Y cannot be equal: after removing the common 2-adic factor, equal valuations would leave two odd legs.
Thus
  epsilon_0=1,
  epsilon_1=1 iff X<Y,
  epsilon_2=1 iff Y<X.
Exactly one of epsilon_1,epsilon_2 is1, so
  epsilon_0+epsilon_1+epsilon_2=2.


Case B: x odd.
Then X=0 and E,Y>0, with E!=Y because e^2+y^2=V^2.
Here
  epsilon_2=0,
and both T0 and T1 compare the same 2-adic leg valuations E versus Y, so
  epsilon_0=epsilon_1 in {0,1}.
Hence the total epsilon sum is0 or2.


Case C: y odd.
Symmetrically
  epsilon_1=0,
  epsilon_0=epsilon_2,
so again the total is0 or2.


Therefore universally
  epsilon_0+epsilon_1+epsilon_2 is even.          (229BK.5)


RESULT_229BK_THREE_MACRO_GAP_EPSILON_SUM_EVEN=PROVED_EXACT.


5. Eight exact integer-square products
Define the six positive macro Euclid gaps
  W0^-:=UV-eR,   W0^+:=UV+eR,
  W1^-:=zV-ex,   W1^+:=zV+ex,
  W2^-:=zU-ey,   W2^+:=zU+ey.                    (229BK.6)


Each minus gap is positive because it is hypotenuse minus a positive leg in an integral Pythagorean triple.


By (229BK.3),
  Wj^sigma = 2^epsilon_j Gj (r_j^sigma)^2
for sigma in {-,+}.


Therefore for ANY independent sign choice
  (sigma0,sigma1,sigma2) in {-,+}^3,
we have
  W0^sigma0 W1^sigma1 W2^sigma2
   = 2^(epsilon0+epsilon1+epsilon2)
     (G0G1G2)
     (r_0^sigma0 r_1^sigma1 r_2^sigma2)^2.


Using229BI
  G0G1G2=(C0C+C-)^2
and (229BK.5), the right side is an exact square:
  W0^sigma0 W1^sigma1 W2^sigma2
   =
  [ 2^((epsilon0+epsilon1+epsilon2)/2)
    C0 C+ C-
    r_0^sigma0 r_1^sigma1 r_2^sigma2 ]^2.         (229BK.7)


Thus all eight positive integers obtained by choosing plus/minus independently are perfect squares.


In particular
  (UV-eR)(zV-ex)(zU-ey) is a square,              (229BK.8)
and
  (UV+eR)(zV+ex)(zU+ey) is a square.              (229BK.9)


RESULT_229BK_ALL_EIGHT_MACRO_SIGN_PRODUCTS_ARE_INTEGER_SQUARES=PROVED_EXACT.


This is a full 2-adic completion of the odd squareclass triangle, not merely an odd-prime support statement.


6. Full squarefree-kernel triangle including the prime 2
Set
  kappa_j := sf(Wj^-), j=0,1,2.                   (229BK.10)


Because W0^- W1^- W2^- is a square, the product
  kappa_0 kappa_1 kappa_2
is a square. Since the kappa_j are squarefree, every prime, including2, occurs in either zero or exactly two of the kappa_j.


Define
  D_- := gcd(kappa_0,kappa_1),
  D_+ := gcd(kappa_0,kappa_2),
  D_0 := gcd(kappa_1,kappa_2).                    (229BK.11)


Then D_0,D_+,D_- are pairwise coprime squarefree positive integers and exactly
  kappa_0 = D_+ D_-,
  kappa_1 = D_- D_0,
  kappa_2 = D_+ D_0.                              (229BK.12)


The odd parts of D_0,D_+,D_- are exactly the229BI squarefree packet contents coming from C0,C+,C- respectively. Equation (229BK.12) canonically routes the prime2 as well, without identifying it with the separately normalized canonical Hilbert 2-adic bits of229AG.


RESULT_229BK_FULL_SQUAREFREE_MACRO_GAP_TRIANGLE_INCLUDING_2=PROVED_EXACT.


Operationally, the three scalar gaps alone recover the complete squarefree packet incidence:
  D_- = gcd(sf(W0^-),sf(W1^-)),
  D_+ = gcd(sf(W0^-),sf(W2^-)),
  D_0 = gcd(sf(W1^-),sf(W2^-)).                  (229BK.13)


This gives a scalar-only theorem interface that no longer requires node labels to reconstruct the full squarefree support triangle.


7. Exact archimedean ordering of the three minus gaps
The current receiver
  W0^-=UV-eR
has a further global property: it is always the strict minimum of the three minus gaps.


Use the rationalized Pythagorean-gap forms:
  W0^- = x^2 y^2/(UV+eR),
  W1^- = y^2 R^2/(zV+ex),
  W2^- = x^2 R^2/(zU+ey).                        (229BK.14)


For W0^-<W1^-, after cancelling y^2 it suffices to show
  x^2(zV+ex) < R^2(UV+eR).
The UV/V term is strict because
  R>x, R>z, U>x
imply
  R^2 U > x^2 z,
hence
  R^2UV > x^2zV.
Also
  eR^3 > ex^3.
Thus the displayed inequality is strict.


Symmetrically
  W0^-<W2^-.


Moreover
  W1^- - W2^-
    = z(V-U)+e(y-x).                              (229BK.15)
Since
  V^2-U^2=y^2-x^2,
V-U has the same sign as y-x. Therefore
  sign(W1^--W2^-)=sign(y-x).                      (229BK.16)


Hence:
  W0^- < min(W1^-,W2^-),
and among W1^-,W2^- the ordering exactly follows y versus x.


RESULT_229BK_W0_IS_STRICT_GLOBAL_MINIMUM_MACRO_MINUS_GAP=PROVED.
RESULT_229BK_W1_W2_ORDER_EQUALS_y_x_ORDER=PROVED.


8. Consequence for the current theorem interface
The current large-K gate still uses
  sf_odd(W0^-)=sf_odd(G0)
from229AR and is not closed by229BK.


However229BK adds a new exact global receiver:
positive physical endpoints map to ordered scalar triples
  (W0^-,W1^-,W2^-)
satisfying simultaneously
  W0^-<min(W1^-,W2^-),
  W0^-W1^-W2^-=square,
  full squarefree packet decomposition (229BK.12),
  exact R-height inherited from the original endpoint.


A future theorem may therefore attack REALIZED scalar triples on this square-product locus rather than arbitrary two-color CRT assignments.


This is genuinely global information: the square relation includes the 2-adic place and couples all three macro triples simultaneously.


But it does NOT itself provide a population saving. The odd-prime support part is compatible with229BI/BJ, so one must not recharge it as an independent sieve condition.


CURRENT_PREFERRED_NEW_INTERNAL_INTERFACE:
FULL_MACRO_GAP_SQUARE_PRODUCT_OCCUPANCY:
count physical ordered triples
  W0<W1,W2,
  W0W1W2=square,
whose full squarefree-kernel triangle is generated by the physical endpoint and whose W0 odd kernel exceeds the one-third threshold, preserving exact R-height and selector equations.


Parallel retained routes:
(A)229BJ global realized-modulus/selector-height saving beyond local color entropy;
(B)229BF removal of the one-per-outer floor;
(C)229AX occupied-support count;
(D)229AR direct W0 tail.


9. Firewalls
DO NOT:
- treat the square-product relation as an independent odd-prime local sieve on top of229BI; its odd support is the same triangle;
- replace the exact physical image by all positive integer triples with square product;
- infer a count merely from W0 being the smallest gap;
- identify the full D_0,D_+,D_- 2-adic routing with229AG canonical Hilbert parity bits without a separate adapter;
- alter authority/credit/gate/closure from this structural theorem.


10. State
No perfect-cuboid existence/nonexistence conclusion is claimed.
No endpoint population exponent is claimed.
No global counting credit is assigned.

-229AD exact six content buckets, h,c12,c21 odd, pairwise coprimality;
-229AR primitive macro-gap Euclid factorization and epsilon convention;
-229BI exact three macro contents and G0G1G2 square;
-229BJ local-color exponent firewall.


The parity proof and eight square-product identities are direct deductions from these retained exact statements. No external theorem is used.
No physical perfect-cuboid endpoint enumeration is used.

  Z0∩Z1 <-> C-=a c21,

with unique prime-by-prime color allocation for every odd squarefree k|G0.


The unresolved question is whether this two-color refinement, by itself or together with a rule that restricts allowed color patterns, improves the local modulus exponent beyond the229AH codimension-two scale.

- each of the three Hilbert colors has exactly the same local cardinality;
- summing all color patterns recovers the uncolored radical-center local mass exactly;

2. Six node blocks and split/unrestricted type
Retain229BI's six 8-node geometric blocks
  N_ex, N_ey, N_eR, N_xy, N_xR, N_yR,
which are the six triple-branch lifts making the 48 A1 nodes of X_pc.

  N_eR <-> h,

  h,c12,c21 have odd support only at primes p==1 mod4,

Thus for every good odd prime p:
  #N_ex(F_p)=#N_ey(F_p)=#N_xy(F_p)=8,            (229BJ.2)
and
  #N_eR(F_p)=#N_xR(F_p)=#N_yR(F_p)
    = 8 if p==1 mod4,
    = 0 if p==3 mod4.                             (229BJ.3)

3. Exact F_p size of each Hilbert color

  K_- := Z0∩Z1 = N_ey ∪ N_xR <-> C-=a c21,
  K_+ := Z0∩Z2 = N_ex ∪ N_yR <-> C+=b c12,

RESULT_229BJ_FULL_NODE_LOCUS_COUNT=48_SPLIT_24_INERT_EXACT.


5. Fixed-color squarefree-modulus CRT mass
Let k be an odd squarefree modulus composed only of good primes.


For each p|k, a Z0-color choice is
  chi(p) in {-,+},
meaning reduction modulo p is required to lie in K_- or K_+.


Let
  c(p):=#K_-(F_p)=#K_+(F_p)
so
  c(p)=16 for p==1 mod4,
  c(p)=8  for p==3 mod4.                          (229BJ.9)


For a fixed complete color pattern
  chi:{p:p|k}->{-,+},
Chinese remainder gives the exact number of local colored residue tuples
  M_col(k;chi)
    = product_{p|k} c(p).                         (229BJ.10)


Crucially this number is independent of chi.


The uncolored Z0 condition has local residue mass
  M_uncol(k)
    = product_{p|k} #Z0(F_p)
    = product_{p|k} 2c(p)
    = 2^{omega(k)} product_{p|k} c(p).            (229BJ.11)


The 2^{omega(k)} different color patterns are disjoint prime-by-prime and exhaust the uncolored Z0 condition. Hence EXACTLY
  sum_chi M_col(k;chi)
    = M_uncol(k).                                 (229BJ.12)

This is stronger than saying the color split fails to change codimension: before any global arithmetic/height restriction is imposed, the two-color decomposition is an exact partition with no local mass loss whatsoever.

Suppose, counterfactually in favor of the method, that some color rule retains only
  A(k)
complete color patterns out of all 2^{omega(k)} patterns.


If the rule changes nothing else in the local residue classes, its exact local mass relative to the uncolored center is
  A(k)/2^{omega(k)}.                              (229BJ.13)


The strongest nonempty color-only restriction is A(k)=1, which gives
  2^{-omega(k)}.                                 (229BJ.14)


But for squarefree k,
  2^{omega(k)} = k^{o(1)}

  2^{omega(k)} <<_epsilon k^epsilon.             (229BJ.15)

  2^{-omega(k)} = k^{-o(1)},                     (229BJ.16)
and in particular there is no fixed eta>0 for which a one-pattern-per-modulus color rule universally supplies

relative saving.


Thus a codimension-two incidence scale
  k^{-2+o(1)}
cannot be upgraded by color selection alone to
  k^{-2-eta}
for any fixed eta>0.

This subsumes the finite-character warning of229AI in the specific exact229BI nodal-color model: even an idealized perfect color selector is only subpower unless it also changes which primes/moduli/physical points are globally realizable.

ordinary codimension-two squarefree-modulus behavior is quantitatively below the one-third divisor-union requirement.


229BJ now rules out a broad attempted repair:
  codimension-two local sieve

  #{P in current positive primitive Stage37 endpoints:
      R(P)<=B,
      K_*(P):=sf(gcd(eR,xy))>B^(1/3-delta)}

Retain229BG's fixed canonical perfect-cuboid surface X_pc in P^6, exact standard sup-height H_inf(P)=R, and retain229AH's exact radical center on the full selector surface.

The strongest existing internal weapons are:

On every exact physical endpoint
  (eR)^2+(xy)^2=(UV)^2,
G_*=gcd(eR,xy) is the exact content of this macro Pythagorean triple, and
  W_-:=UV-eR=2^epsilon G_* r_-^2,

  K_odd=sf_odd(L_-L_+), L_±=O(B).

RESULT_229BH_ARSENAL_DIRECT_CLOSURE=NONE_FOUND.

3. Audit B — current number-theory literature


3.1 GCD-height theorems
Yu Yasufuku, “GCD inequalities arising from codimension-2 blowups”, BLMS 58 (2026), e70349, DOI 10.1112/blms.70349:
unconditionally proves a weaker Silverman/Vojta-type GCD-height inequality using Ru–Vojta/Subspace-theorem machinery.

WRONG_POPULATION / MISSING_ADAPTER.


3.2 Squarefree/power-free binary-form literature
Bhargava–Shankar–Wang, “Squarefree values of polynomial discriminants II”, Forum Math. Pi 13 (2025) e17, and Stanley Yao Xiao, “Power-Free Values of Binary Forms and the Global Determinant Method”, IMRN 2017:

3.3 Geometric/rational-point sieves
Browning–Loughran, “Sieving rational points on varieties”, Trans. AMS 371 (2019):
gives upper-bound sieves for rational points on suitable varieties, with applications to thin sets, local solubility, and friable points; quadrics receive sharper Selberg-sieve estimates.
The issue is not availability of a generic sieve formalism. The Stage37 missing input is a same-physical selector-conditioned distribution theorem with enough growing-modulus uniformity and the correct absolute B-exponent.


Zhizhong Huang, “Equidistribution of rational points and the geometric sieve for toric varieties”, arXiv:2111.01509:
proves effective adelic equidistribution and an Ekedahl-type geometric sieve on smooth projective SPLIT toric varieties over Q.
This is the closest theorem species to the229AH codimension-2 radical center, but it does not directly apply to the fixed canonical perfect-cuboid surface X_pc, which229BG identifies as a general-type complete intersection, not a smooth split toric variety. handles toric varieties, including nonsplit situations in the retained Stage37 audit, using universal torsors/harmonic analysis. It supplies base/integral-point counting, not the required selector-conditioned growing squarefree-modulus radical sieve on X_pc.

Buggenhout–Cluckers–Santens–Vermeulen, “Serre's question on thin sets in projective space”, arXiv:2506.13471 (2025):
for a quasi-finite dominant cover f:X->P^n of degree d, gives

and B^n for d>=5.

It does not carry the multiplicative radical event k|gcd(eR,xy), and its scale is nowhere near an absolute o(B^(1/3)) target in the present surface problem. RESULT_229BH_CURRENT_LITERATURE_DIRECT_BLACKBOX=NONE_FOUND.

Retain229BG:
  X_pc subset P^6_[e:x:y:z:R:U:V]

  p|G_*(P)

  K_odd(P)=product_{odd p : P mod p in Z_rad(F_p)} p.  (229BH.8)

This is not a new identity beyond229AH/O; it is the exact theorem-facing formulation that every external sieve must preserve.


4.2 Why an ordinary Ekedahl large-prime sieve is insufficient
The event K_odd>T does NOT imply that one prime p>T divides G_*.

Therefore a theorem controlling only
  exists p>M with P mod p in Z_rad
does not directly control the radical tail.
The needed input is uniform simultaneous local-condition control for SQUAREFREE MODULI.


Define for squarefree odd k
  N_phys(B;k)

         R(P)<=B, k|G_*(P)}.                           (229BH.9)

cannot close the current divisor-union budget at sigma=2; even sigma=3 misses in the stated one-third regime.229AH then proved that lifting the selector cover does not increase the radical center above codimension two.
Thus the missing theorem must exploit GLOBAL SELECTOR CORRELATION / OCCUPIED SUPPORT, not merely local codimension.


RESULT_229BH_PREFERRED_EXTERNAL_CONTRACT=
SELECTOR_CONDITIONED_SQUAREFREE_MODULUS_RADICAL_SIEVE:

  + genuinely stronger-than-codimension-only global decay/cancellation
  -> o(B^(1/3)) above K_*>B^(1/3-delta).           (229BH.10)

5.2 Fixed-outer known problem:229BF

  rational/integral points of exact projective height R
  on X_pc
  satisfying a multiplicative codimension-two radical condition.

  MULTIPLICATIVE CODIMENSION-TWO SIEVE INSIDE A DEGREE-FOUR THIN COVER.

- large-square-factor / power-free binary-form problems: wrong tail direction;

- fixed-genus finiteness: no moving-height uniformity;
